In [[mathematics]], a '''unistochastic matrix''' (also called ''unitary-stochastic'') is a [[doubly stochastic matrix]] whose entries are the squares of the absolute values of the entries of some [[unitary matrix]].

A square matrix ''B'' of size ''n'' is doubly stochastic (or ''bistochastic'') if all its entries are non-negative [[real number]]s and each of its rows and columns sum to 1. It is unistochastic if there exists a unitary matrix ''U'' such that

:<math> B_{ij}=|U_{ij}|^2 \text{ for } i,j=1,\dots,n. \, </math>

This definition is analogous to that for an [[orthostochastic matrix]], which is a doubly stochastic matrix whose entries are the squares of the entries in some [[orthogonal matrix]]. Since all orthogonal matrices are necessarily unitary matrices, all orthostochastic matrices are also unistochastic. The converse, however, is not true. First, all 2-by-2 doubly [[Stochastic matrix|stochastic matrices]] are both unistochastic and [[orthostochastic matrix|orthostochastic]], but for larger ''n'' this is not the case. For example, take <math> n=3 </math> and consider the following doubly stochastic matrix:
:<math>
B= \frac{1}{2} 
\begin{bmatrix}
1  & 1 & 0  \\
0  & 1 & 1  \\
1  & 0 & 1   \end{bmatrix}.
</math>
This matrix is not unistochastic, since any two vectors with moduli equal to the square root of the entries of two columns (or rows) of ''B'' cannot be made orthogonal by a suitable choice of phases. For <math display="inline">n > 2</math>, the set of orthostochastic matrices is a [[proper subset]] of the set of unistochastic matrices.

* the set of unistochastic matrices contains all [[permutation matrix|permutation matrices]] and its [[convex hull]] is the [[Birkhoff polytope]] of all doubly stochastic matrices
* for  <math> n \ge 3 </math> this set is not convex
* for  <math> n = 3 </math> the set of [[triangle inequality]] on the moduli of the raw is a sufficient and necessary condition for the unistocasticity  <ref>{{cite journal | last=Fedullo | first=A. | title=On the existence of a Hilbert-space model for finite-valued observables| journal=Il Nuovo Cimento B | publisher=Springer | volume=107 | issue=12 | date=1992-12-01 | issn=1826-9877 | doi=10.1007/BF02722852 | pages=1413–1426| bibcode=1992NCimB.107.1413F }}</ref>
* for  <math> n =3 </math> the set of unistochastic matrices is star--shaped and unistochasticity of any bistochastic matrix ''B'' is implied by a non-negative value of its [[Jarlskog invariant]]<ref>{{cite journal | last=Jarlskog | first=C. | title=Commutator of the Quark Mass Matrices in the Standard Electroweak Model and a Measure of Maximal CP Nonconservation | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=55 | issue=10 | date=1985-09-02 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.55.1039 | pages=1039–1042| pmid=10031712 | bibcode=1985PhRvL..55.1039J }}</ref>
* for  <math> n =3 </math> the relative volume of the set of unistochastic matrices with respect to the [[Birkhoff polytope]] of doubly stochastic matrices is <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Dunkl | first1=Charles | last2=Życzkowski | first2=Karol | title=Volume of the set of unistochastic matrices of order 3 and the mean Jarlskog invariant | journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=50 | issue=12 | year=2009 | issn=0022-2488 | doi=10.1063/1.3272543 | page=123521|arxiv=0909.0116| bibcode=2009JMP....50l3521D }}</ref> <math> 8\pi^2/105 \approx 75.2 \% </math>
* for  <math> n =4 </math> explicit conditions for unistochasticity are not known yet, but there exists a numerical method to verify unistochasticity based on the algorithm by Haagerup <ref>{{cite journal | last1=Rajchel | first1=Grzegorz | last2=Gąsiorowski | first2=Adam | last3=Życzkowski | first3=Karol | title=Robust Hadamard Matrices, Unistochastic Rays in Birkhoff Polytope and Equi-Entangled Bases in Composite Spaces | journal=Mathematics in Computer Science | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=12 | issue=4 | date=2018-09-19 | issn=1661-8270 | doi=10.1007/s11786-018-0384-y | pages=473–490|doi-access=free|arxiv=1804.10715}}</ref>
* The [[Schur-Horn theorem]] is equivalent to the following "weak convexity" property of the set <math> \mathcal{U}_n </math> of unistochastic <math> n \times n </math> matrices: for any vector <math> v \in \mathbb{R}^n </math> the set <math> \mathcal{U}_nv </math> is the convex hull of the set of vectors obtained by all permutations of the entries of the vector <math> v </math> (the permutation polytope generated by the vector <math> v </math>).
* The set of <math> n \times n </math> unistochastic matrices <math> \mathcal{U}_n \subset \mathbb{R}^{(n-1)^2} </math> has a nonempty interior. The unistochastic matrix corresponding to the unitary <math> n \times n </math> matrix with the entries <math> U_{ij} = \delta_{ij} + \frac{\theta-1}{n} </math>, where <math> |\theta|=1 </math> and <math> \theta \neq \pm 1 </math>, is an interior point of <math> \mathcal{U}_n </math>.
